subject: AWS reseller pilot — one-time SKU stacking concession request
messages:
Date: Mon, 16 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -07:00
From: Elena Morales <elena@cloudharbor.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Amy Liu <amy@amazon.com>, finance@cloudharbor.com
Subject: Request: single-use SKU stacking concession for reseller pilot

Hi Irene,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CloudHarbor liked the latency/cost profile. We're preparing an AWS reseller pilot (pilot name: MAAP) and want to publish a bundled Marketplace offer combining two SKUs (core inference + inference-engineering support).

AWS listing rules mean we need a single SKU price to show in the marketplace. To keep the initial price competitive and preserve our margin, we're requesting a one-time stacking concession that effectively combines the two SKUs at a 20% off list bundle for the first six months of the pilot. The economics are temporary and apply only to the CloudHarbor pilot cohort (~$180k TCV expected over 12 months if pilot converts).

Attached is a short SOW and pilot timeline. Can Redwood approve a one-time concession for this pilot? If so, we can proceed with DocuSign and marketplace listing.

Attachments: CloudHarbor_MAAP_SOW.pdf (2 pages)

Thanks,
Elena Morales
Head of Strategic Partnerships
CloudHarbor
elena@cloudharbor.com
+1 415-555-0182

Subject: Re: Request: single-use SKU stacking concession for reseller pilot

Hi Elena — thanks for the SOW, looks reasonable. I'm looping in Ben from Deal Desk and Vanessa from Marketplace Ops to evaluate a one-time concession.

Quick context for Ben/Vanessa: CloudHarbor is requesting a 20% bundled price for two SKUs for the first 6 months of a pilot (pilot TCV ~ $180k; expected ARR if converted ~$150k). They need a single SKU for AWS listing that preserves perceived value. The ask is single-use (one listing/one pilot) and limited term.

Next steps I propose:
- Ben: can you review for approval or an approved alternative (promotional credit or pilot coupon)?
- Vanessa: marketplace constraints (taxonomy/sku rules) + any listing work we need to do.
- Elena: if approved, please confirm the DocuSign contact and we'll send a term sheet.

Irene
Irene Choi
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 10:02:00 -07:00
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: single-use SKU stacking concession for reseller pilot

Irene — thanks for the context. Reviewed the SOW and pilot economics. A few notes from Deal Desk:

- One-time concession of 20% off bundled list for 6 months is within the scope of a strategic reseller pilot, provided we add controls.
- Conditions we need:
  1) The concession is explicitly time-bound (6 months) and tied to the listed pilot SKUs only.
  2) CloudHarbor must sign the one-time concession term sheet and NDA addendum.
  3) We cap total concession exposure at $36k (20% of pilot TCV).
  4) Finance must approve revenue recognition treatment (cc Kim).

Alternative we can offer (if legal/finance push back): grant CloudHarbor a promotional credit applied in Marketplace (credit expires after 9 months) rather than changing the listed SKU price. That keeps pricing standard and lets us track the spend.

I've drafted a short term sheet and a spreadsheet with the math — attaching pricing-model.xlsx.

Ben
Ben Carter
Director, Deal Desk
ben_carter@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 17 Aug 2027 14:28:00 -07:00
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.com>
Subject: Re: Request: single-use SKU stacking concession for reseller pilot

Ben/Team — Finance reviewed and provisionally approves the one-time concession exposure cap ($36k) if the term sheet includes:
- Clear start/end dates for concession
- Explicit non-recurring clause (pilot-only)
- Reporting cadence: CloudHarbor must share monthly usage reports for the pilot, we will reconcile credits against billed Marketplace invoices.

If CloudHarbor prefers the promotional credit route, that also works but delays listing publication by ~5 business days while we set up the credit instrument.

Kimberly Park
Sr. Manager, Finance Ops
kimberly_park@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 18 Aug 2027 13:03:00 -07:00
From: Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Approved: one-time SKU stacking concession for CloudHarbor MAAP pilot (term sheet attached)

Hi Elena — good news. Deal Desk and Finance have approved a one-time, pilot-only SKU stacking concession as requested with the following terms:

- Concession: 20% off combined list price for the two SKUs in the MAAP pilot.
- Term: 6 months from Go-Live date (Go-Live to be defined in signed DocuSign term sheet).
- Exposure cap: $36,000 total concession value.
- Obligations: CloudHarbor to supply monthly usage reports and to adhere to the pilot SOW.
- Implementation: Redwood Marketplace Ops will publish the single bundled SKU for the MAAP pilot; if preferred we can alternatively apply a promotional credit (CloudHarbor to confirm).

Attached: one-time-concession-term-sheet.pdf (please sign via DocuSign)
DocuSign link: https://app.docusign.com/1234-aws-concession
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.example.com/deal/12345 (deal id RWF-2027-014)

Please confirm the DocuSign contact and expected Go-Live date so we can schedule the listing work (Vanessa will own).

Thanks and looking forward to the pilot — happy to jump on a quick call if you want to run through the term sheet.

Best,
